name.text: Counting Words with Specific Letter Constraints

questiontext.text:
How many {@word1@}-letter words can be formed from the letters of the word {@word@} if the word must begin with \(A\) and end with \(A\) and no letter may be repeated.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

We need to form a {@word1@} letter word from the word {@word@} where the first and last letters are already selected

From the remaining {@wordlength1-2@} letters we choose the three middle letters:

[[ if test='wordlength1=6' ]]

\(\displaystyle 4 \times 3 \times 2 = \frac {4!}{2!}={@factorial(4)/factorial(2)@}\)

[[ elif test='wordlength1=7 ' ]]

\(\displaystyle 5 \times 4 \times 3 = \frac {5!}{2!}={@factorial(5)/factorial(2)@}\)

[[ else ]]

\(\displaystyle 6 \times 5 \times 4 = \frac {6!}{2!}={@factorial(6)/factorial(2)@}\)

[[/ if]]
